# Capacity, scaling laws and cost {#sec-capacity}

**On the DrivAerML Surface task, cells stop paying at 100,000, width and
depth pay until a shared floor near 0.040, and compute should go to cases
below about 200 and to width above it.** The scope is one dataset and one
task throughout, at two budgets: the reporting protocol of 200,000 cells
per case and, for the capacity and scaling studies, 100,000 cells, labeled
in every caption; the metric is the area-weighted relative L2 of surface
pressure in float32 over the 48 DrivAerML validation cars (@sec-metrics),
every ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA, and the capacity and scaling lanes span
widths from 192 to 1,536 and depths from 12 to 48 layers at 256 slices,
each labeled with its width, depth and rate; none of them is the reference
configuration (width 512 with 512 slices, @sec-using-config), which sits on
these axes as one more point, so every "ISLA" in this chapter is the lane
its row or caption names.

```{python}
#| label: setup-capacity
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
ISOJ = J("isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json")
SHL = J("scalehl_2026-09-26.json")  # SCALE-HL: the same ladders on the 510-wing HiLiftAeroML rung (100,000 cells; ROUTE-NORM cosine lanes beside)
ISO = ISOJ["configurations"]
# the 384-wide ISLA (384 x 12, 256 slices, 5e-4) at the reporting protocol, its 24-layer depth variant and GeoTransolver-512
REF = J("ref_surface_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
refm = lambda k, f="pressure_l2": REF[k]["fields"][f]["mean"]
P2A = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")["arms"]
TENK = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")["tenk_reference"]
QV = J("quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json")["arms"]  # the stratified and 40,000-cell draws of one pair of 435-car checkpoints
GT256_435 = P2A["gt_unit_lr3e3"]["pressure_mean"]
RB = J("refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json"); RBS = RB["summary"]; RBX = RB["learning_curve_exponents"]
```

## Cells per case are flat above 100,000 {#sec-equal-budget}


**Above 100,000 cells per case the error of every architecture is flat in
the cell count, so a comparison between models is read at matched memory
or matched parameters, never down a column of cell counts.**
@tbl-cells-ladder trains ISLA at 192 wide and GeoTransolver and Transolver
at 256 wide, each at its own best learning rate, from 100,000 to 600,000 cells per case and scores
every lane on the one instrument. The only variable down a column is
therefore how many surface cells a case is sampled to. The fitted exponent
of error against cells is
`{python} f"{ISOJ['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_isla']:.2f}"` for ISLA
and `{python} f"{ISOJ['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_gt']:.2f}"` for
GeoTransolver, and doubling the schedule from 500 to 1,000 epochs at
200,000 cells moves ISLA-192 by
`{python} f"{100 * abs(ISO['isla|w192|c200k|lr1e-3|ep1000']['pressure_l2_mean'] / ISO['isla|w192|c200k|lr1e-3|ep500']['pressure_l2_mean'] - 1):.2f}"`%
and GeoTransolver-256 by
`{python} f"{100 * abs(ISO['gt_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep1000']['pressure_l2_mean'] / ISO['gt_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500']['pressure_l2_mean'] - 1):.2f}"`%,
so the protocol is converged and neither cells nor epochs are a lever past
the reporting protocol. What buys accuracy past 100,000 cells is width and
depth (@sec-shared-floor).

### Below the protocol the cell count still pays {#sec-deficit-anatomy}

The step from smaller counts up to the protocol is not flat, and the part
of it that is ISLA's own is quadrature noise: ISLA's slice states are
measure-weighted means over the drawn cells (@sec-isla-quadrature), so at
a small count they inherit more of the draw's variance than the baselines'
unweighted aggregates do. Two readings of one pair of 435-car checkpoints
locate it. A stratified draw of the same 10,000 cells, which keeps the
inclusion law and only spreads the cells, moves GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA from
`{python} f"{QV['gt_unit']['unif']['10000'] / QV['isla_ref']['unif']['10000']:.3f}"`
to
`{python} f"{QV['gt_unit']['strat']['10000']['mean'] / QV['isla_ref']['strat']['10000']['mean']:.3f}"`,
an independent 40,000-cell draw moves it to
`{python} f"{QV['gt_unit']['unif']['40000'] / QV['isla_ref']['unif']['40000']:.3f}"`,
and at 200,000 cells the same configuration reads
`{python} f"{TENK['gt_unit'] / TENK['isla']:.2f}"`
at 10,000 cells against
`{python} f"{min(P2A['gt_unit_lr1e3']['pressure_mean'], P2A['gt_unit_lr3e3']['pressure_mean']) / P2A['isla']['pressure_mean']:.3f}"`
at the protocol. For deployment the consequence is the recommendation of
@sec-using-sampler: use the stratified draw, or more cells.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cells-ladder
#| output: asis
ladder = [("ISLA, 192 wide, 1e-3", "isla", 192, "1e-3", (100, 200, 400, 600)),
          ("GeoTransolver, 256 wide, 3e-3", "gt_unit", 256, "3e-3", (100, 200, 400)),
          ("Transolver, 256 wide, 3e-3", "transolver_unit", 256, "3e-3", (100, 200, 400))]
out = "| architecture, width, learning rate | cells per case | surface pressure error (seed 42 / 43) | mean | relative to the same model at 100,000 |\n|---|--:|---|--:|--:|\n"
for lab, m, w, lr, cells in ladder:
    base = ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c100k|lr{lr}|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"]
    for n in cells:
        c = ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{n}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]
        s = " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in c["pressure_l2_seeds"])
        out += f"| {lab} | {n},000 | {s} | **{c['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}** | {c['pressure_l2_mean'] / base:.3f} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The cell-count ladder on the DrivAerML Surface task (435 training cars, 500 epochs): area-weighted relative L2 "
      "of surface pressure over the 48 validation cars, scored in float32 at 200,000 cells whatever the training count, "
      "two seeds. Every model trains and is scored at the same cell count, ISLA at 192 wide and the baselines at 256 wide, each at its "
      "own best rate. The last column divides the row's seed mean by the same model's at 100,000 training cells (below 1 "
      "is better). How to read this: a within-model control of the training cell count. The rows differ by under 1% "
      "within a column, so the cell count above 100,000 is not an axis of accuracy for any of the three. It is not a "
      "comparison between architectures (their rows differ in width and parameters). Data: "
      "results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json. {#tbl-cells-ladder}")
```

## The capacity floor {#sec-shared-floor}


**At 435 DrivAerML cars both architectures reach the same accuracy floor
in surface pressure, and ISLA reaches it along its depth axis with about
half of GeoTransolver's parameters. At matched parameters near 140M the
two are identical within a seed spread.** The budget is 100,000 cells per
case, where cells have stopped paying for every model (@tbl-cells-ladder),
so what remains is capacity. The one 200,000-cell ISLA lane at the floor is
shown beside its 100,000-cell twin. Two ladders feed the section. A width
ladder takes ISLA from 192 to 1,536 wide and GeoTransolver from 256 to
2,048 wide, each width at the better of the learning rates run for it. A
depth ladder takes ISLA at 384 wide from 12 to 48 layers and
GeoTransolver at 512 wide from 12 to 24. Every lane trains for 500 epochs
with two seeds and is scored in float32 at 200,000 cells. @tbl-floor
collects the lanes at the floor, and @fig-capacity puts every ladder on
one axis of parameter count.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-floor
#| output: asis
CAPI = J("cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
CFG = J("cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
RNC = J("routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
EXT = J("routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json")["configurations"]
RP = J("routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json")["configurations"]
# trainable parameters of ISLA by width at 12 layers and 256 slices, as counted by the training script
PW = {c["width"]: c["params"] for c in CFG.values() if c["model"] == "isla" and c["depth"] == 12 and c["slices"] == 256}
def rec(mean_, seeds, params, mem=None, est=False):
    return dict(pressure_l2_mean=mean_, pressure_l2_seeds=seeds, params=params, peak_mem_gb=mem, params_estimated=est)
c384 = RNC["cars|cos|w384|lr5e-4"]
p200 = RP["cars|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4|c200k"]
# (architecture, width x layers, training cells, learning rate, record)
floor_rows = [
    ("ISLA", "384 × 12", "100,000", "5e-4", rec(c384["mean"], c384["seeds"], PW[384])),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 24", "100,000", "5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 24", "200,000", "5e-4", rec(p200["pressure_l2_mean"], p200["pressure_l2_seeds"], EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["params"])),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 48", "100,000", "2.5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "512 × 12", "200,000", "3e-3", ISO["gt_unit|w512|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "512 × 24", "100,000", "3e-3", CAPI["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "1,024 × 12", "100,000", "1e-3", CAPI["gt|w1024|d12|s256|lr1e3"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "2,048 × 12", "100,000", "1e-3", EXT["gt|w2048|d12|lr1e-3"]),
]
# the floor band: the span of the best two lanes of each architecture in this table
def best_two(arch):
    return sorted(r[4]["pressure_l2_mean"] for r in floor_rows if r[0] == arch)[:2]
FLOOR = best_two("ISLA") + best_two("GeoTransolver")
floor_lo, floor_hi = min(FLOOR), max(FLOOR)
out = "| architecture | width × layers | parameters | training cells | learning rate | surface pressure error, mean (seeds) | peak memory [GB] |\n|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|\n"
for arch, shape, cells, lr, c in floor_rows:
    params = f"{c['params'] / 1e6:.0f}M" + (" (estimated)" if c.get("params_estimated") else "")
    seeds = " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in c["pressure_l2_seeds"])
    memv = c.get("peak_mem_gb")
    out += f"| {arch} | {shape} | {params} | {cells} | {lr} | **{c['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}** ({seeds}) | {'not logged' if memv is None else f'{memv:.0f}'} |\n"
print(out)
print(f": The lanes of either architecture at or near the floor on the DrivAerML Surface task: 435 training cars, "
      f"100,000 training cells per case except the two 200,000-cell rows, all scored in float32 at 200,000 cells on the "
      f"48 validation cars, 500 epochs, two seeds. The floor band of @fig-capacity is the span of the best two lanes of "
      f"each architecture in this table, {floor_lo:.4f} to {floor_hi:.4f}. *Parameters*: trainable, as counted by the "
      f"training script; GeoTransolver-2,048's is extrapolated from its measured 256 to 1,024 ladder. *Peak memory*: "
      f"peak of the logged per-step values on one GB300 where the lane logged it. How to read this: the table names "
      f"the floor and what each model pays to reach it, not a ranking (the errors differ by less than a seed spread). "
      f"Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json, results/cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json, "
      f"results/cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json, results/routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json, "
      f"results/routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json, results/routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json. {{#tbl-floor}}")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-capacity
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Surface-pressure error against trainable parameters on the DrivAerML
#|   Surface task (435 training cars, 48 validation cars, 100,000 cells per
#|   case unless labeled, 500 epochs, float32 at 200,000 cells; two-seed
#|   means with the seeds as short bars). Red: GeoTransolver's width ladder
#|   (filled circles) and its 24-layer lane at 512 wide (open circles,
#|   dotted). Blue: ISLA's width ladder at 12 layers (filled squares),
#|   ISLA's depth ladder at 384 wide (open diamonds, dotted), and the
#|   384-wide, 24-layer configuration trained at 200,000 cells (star). Each
#|   width is at the better of the learning rates run for it. The gray band
#|   is the span of the best two lanes of each architecture, computed from
#|   the lanes of @tbl-floor and written on the band. How to read this: the
#|   x axis is parameters, not memory or time (those are @fig-equal-budget);
#|   GeoTransolver-2,048's count is estimated from the measured 256 to 1,024
#|   ladder; the y axis starts at 0.039, below the floor, and ends at
#|   0.0485, above the widest lane. Data:
#|   results/cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json,
#|   results/routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json,
#|   results/routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json,
#|   results/routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json.
#| fig-alt: "Scatter of validation pressure error against parameter count on a log axis, with ISLA's width and depth ladders in blue and GeoTransolver's in red converging into a gray band near 0.040."
#| code-fold: true
def best_of(cands):
    """(params, mean, seeds) of the lowest-error candidate; candidates are (mean, seeds, params)."""
    m, s, p = min(cands, key=lambda t: t[0]); return p, m, s
def isla_w(w):
    cands = [(c["mean"], c["seeds"], PW[w]) for k, c in RNC.items() if k.startswith(f"cars|cos|w{w}|")]
    cands += [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for k, c in EXT.items() if k.startswith(f"isla|cos|w{w}|d12|")]
    return best_of(cands)
def isla_d(key):
    c = EXT[key]; return c["params"], c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"]
def gt_w(w):
    cands = [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for c in CFG.values() if c["model"] == "gt" and c["width"] == w and c["depth"] == 12]
    cands += [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for k, c in EXT.items() if k.startswith(f"gt|w{w}|d12|")]
    return best_of(cands)
gt_width = [gt_w(w) for w in (256, 512, 1024, 2048)]
c24 = CFG["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]
gt_depth = [gt_w(512), (c24["params"], c24["pressure_l2_mean"], c24["pressure_l2_seeds"])]
isla_width = [isla_w(w) for w in (192, 384, 768, 1024, 1536)]
isla_depth = [isla_w(384), isla_d("isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"), isla_d("isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4")]
isla_200k = (EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["params"], p200["pressure_l2_mean"], p200["pressure_l2_seeds"])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.6, 5.2))
def draw(series, key, label, ls="-", marker=None, mfc=None, ms=7):
    kw = series_kwargs(key, lw=1.8, ms=ms); kw["ls"] = ls; kw["label"] = label
    if marker: kw["marker"] = marker
    if mfc is not None: kw["mfc"] = mfc
    ax.plot([s[0] for s in series], [s[1] for s in series], **kw, zorder=3)
    for x, _, seeds in series:
        ax.plot([x] * len(seeds), seeds, ls="none", marker="_", color=kw["color"], ms=8, mew=1.1, zorder=4)
draw(gt_width, "gt", "GeoTransolver, width 256 → 2,048 (12 layers)")
draw(gt_depth, "gt", "GeoTransolver, 512 wide, 12 → 24 layers", ls=":", mfc="white")
draw(isla_width, "isla_ref", "ISLA, width 192 → 1,536 (12 layers)")
draw(isla_depth, "isla_ref", "ISLA, 384 wide, 12 → 48 layers", ls=":", marker="D", mfc="white")
draw([isla_200k], "isla_ref", "ISLA, 384 wide, 24 layers, trained at 200,000 cells", ls="none", marker="*", ms=13)
ax.axhspan(floor_lo, floor_hi, color=GRID, zorder=0)
ax.text(6.5e6, (floor_lo + floor_hi) / 2, f"the floor: {floor_lo:.4f} to {floor_hi:.4f}", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2, va="center", path_effects=halo())
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(5e6, 1.0e9); ax.set_ylim(0.039, 0.0485)
ax.set_xlabel("trainable parameters [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
ax.set_xticks([1e7, 3e7, 1e8, 3e8, 1e9]); ax.set_xticklabels(["10M", "30M", "100M", "300M", "1B"])
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8.2)
plt.show()
```

Three readings carry the figure.

1. **Width pays, for both, up to about 35M parameters, then GeoTransolver
   keeps paying and ISLA does not.** GeoTransolver's width ladder improves
   by
   `{python} " / ".join(f"{100 * (1 - b[1] / a[1]):.1f}%" for a, b in zip(gt_width[:-1], gt_width[1:]))`
   per doubling from 256 to 2,048 wide. The last doubling buys the size of
   a seed spread. ISLA's width ladder improves by
   `{python} f"{100 * (1 - isla_width[1][1] / isla_width[0][1]):.1f}%"`
   from 192 to 384 wide, is flat to 768 and declines after. Width is
   therefore not ISLA's axis past 35M parameters.
2. **Depth is ISLA's axis on this dataset, and it pays a little.** At 384
   wide, 24 layers read
   `{python} f"{isla_depth[1][1]:.4f}"` at
   `{python} f"{isla_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M"` parameters and 48 layers
   `{python} f"{isla_depth[2][1]:.4f}"` at
   `{python} f"{isla_depth[2][0] / 1e6:.0f}M"`. The 24-layer configuration
   trained at 200,000 cells reads `{python} f"{isla_200k[1]:.4f}"`,
   within
   `{python} f"{100 * abs(isla_200k[1] / isla_depth[1][1] - 1):.1f}%"`
   of its 100,000-cell twin, so the floor is not a property of the
   100,000-cell budget. GeoTransolver's depth lane (512 wide, 24 layers)
   reaches the same band at `{python} f"{gt_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M"`
   parameters. At the reporting protocol the 24-layer configuration at
   384 wide is
   `{python} f"{100 * (1 - refm('isla_r2|dr435') / refm('isla_r1|dr435')):.1f}%"`
   better than 12 layers at 384 wide on the cars and
   `{python} f"{100 * abs(1 - refm('isla_r2|hl35') / refm('isla_r1|hl35')):.1f}%"`
   apart from it on the 35-wing rung, both inside a 1.5% band, at twice
   the step time and memory (@tbl-isla-cost); the reference selection
   spent ISLA's memory on width and slices instead (@sec-scoreboard-200k)
   (results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json).
3. **Both architectures reach the same floor, and ISLA reaches it with
   fewer parameters.** At matched parameters of about 140M the two are
   identical within a seed spread (GeoTransolver-1,024 ÷ ISLA-384×48 =
   `{python} f"{gt_width[2][1] / isla_depth[2][1]:.3f}"`). ISLA at 384×24
   sits `{python} f"{100 * (isla_depth[1][1] / gt_width[2][1] - 1):.1f}%"`
   above GeoTransolver-1,024 at
   `{python} f"{100 * isla_depth[1][0] / gt_width[2][0]:.0f}%"` of its
   parameters.

The shared floor is measured on DrivAerML; on the wings it is not
established (@sec-limits). @tbl-scalehl puts the same readings, and the
memory frontier, on the 510-wing HiLiftAeroML rung: two reproduce and
three do not.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scalehl
#| output: asis
SA = SHL["arms"]
rows = [
    ("cells stop paying at 100,000",
     f"GeoTransolver-256 {SHL['bars']['cells_flat']['gt_256_c100k_over_c200k_lr3e3']:.2f}, Transolver-256 {SHL['bars']['cells_flat']['transolver_256_c100k_over_c200k']:.2f}, ISLA {SHL['bars']['cells_flat']['isla_cos_192_c100k_over_c200k']:.2f} (100,000 ÷ 200,000 cells)",
     "**reproduces**"),
    ("width pays for both architectures",
     f"ISLA 384 ÷ 192 = {SA['isla_cos_384_lr1e3_c100k']['seed_means']['pressure_l2'] / SA['isla_cos_192_c100k']['seed_means']['pressure_l2']:.2f}, but GeoTransolver 512 ÷ 256 = {SHL['bars']['width_carries']['gt_512_over_256']:.2f}",
     "**does not**: width pays for ISLA and not for GeoTransolver here"),
    ("ISLA's width turns over at 384",
     f"768 ÷ 384 = {SHL['bars']['turnover']['isla_768_over_384']:.2f}",
     "**does not**: no turnover on the wings"),
    ("the deficit is width-independent",
     f"GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA {SA['gt_256_c100k']['seed_means']['pressure_l2'] / SA['isla_cos_192_c100k']['seed_means']['pressure_l2']:.2f} at 192 wide and {SA['gt_512_c100k']['seed_means']['pressure_l2'] / SA['isla_cos_384_lr1e3_c100k']['seed_means']['pressure_l2']:.2f} at 384",
     "**reproduces**"),
    ("ISLA holds the memory frontier",
     f"GeoTransolver-512 at {SA['gt_512_c100k']['mem_peak_gb']:.0f} GB scores {SA['gt_512_c100k']['seed_means']['pressure_l2']:.4f} against ISLA-768 at {SA['isla_768_c100k']['mem_peak_gb']:.0f} GB at {SA['isla_768_c100k']['seed_means']['pressure_l2']:.4f}",
     "**does not**: GeoTransolver holds the wing frontier"),
]
out = "| the DrivAerML reading | what the 510-wing rung measures | verdict |\n|---|---|---|\n"
for r in rows: out += "| " + " | ".join(r) + " |\n"
print(out)
print(": The same ladders on the 510-wing HiLiftAeroML rung: surface-pressure area-weighted relative L2 on the 180 validation cases, "
      "float32, 100,000 cells per case, 500 epochs, two seeds, ISLA under cosine routing at the width rule's rate and GeoTransolver at "
      "3e-3. How to read this: each row restates a DrivAerML reading of this chapter and says whether the wing rung reproduces it; the "
      "cells and deficit rows do and the width and frontier rows do not, so the width turnover at 384 and the memory frontier are "
      "DrivAerML facts. Data: results/scalehl_2026-09-26.json. {#tbl-scalehl}")
```

## The memory and time frontier {#sec-review-frontier}

**Below about 70 GB of training memory and 0.3 s per step, the best ISLA
lane at or under each budget is at least as accurate as the best
GeoTransolver lane. Above that budget GeoTransolver's widest lanes sit
about 1% below ISLA's best cost-logged lane.** The section's grid is a
width-and-cells study at 100,000 cells. The 384-wide lanes of
@sec-cost-sweep at the reporting protocol sit on the same frontier. The instrument here is the same grid of
lanes as @tbl-cells-ladder and the width ladders, with every lane's peak
memory and step time read from its own training log. The step time is
reported two ways, because at these sizes the input pipeline (one case per
GPU step) sets the median step rather than the network. The tenth
percentile of the logged steps is the *GPU-floor step time*, the cost of
the network alone. The median is the wall clock a user waits.
@fig-equal-budget draws error against both costs with each model's
frontier, the best error attainable at or under a budget. @tbl-equal-budget
lists every lane. One limit bounds the claim. The frontier is a statement
about the cost-logged lanes only, and ISLA's depth ladder, which reaches
the floor at 68M parameters (@sec-shared-floor), carries no cost log. The
ISLA frontier above 70 GB is therefore an upper bound on what the
architecture can do there.

```{python}
#| label: fig-equal-budget
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Error against training cost for every cost-logged lane of the
#|   cell-count ladder and the width and depth ladders on the DrivAerML
#|   Surface task (435 cars, 500 epochs, two-seed means with the seeds as
#|   short bars; trained at 100,000 to 600,000 cells per case, every lane
#|   scored in float32 at 200,000 cells). Top: peak GPU memory per device;
#|   bottom: GPU-floor step time (the tenth percentile of the logged steps).
#|   The step lines are each model's frontier, the best error attainable at
#|   or under a budget; only the lanes that set a frontier are labeled,
#|   width x training cells (L24 for the 24-layer GeoTransolver), and every
#|   lane is listed in @tbl-equal-budget; GeoTransolver's recipe default
#|   (256 wide, 200,000 cells) is ringed. How to read this: below about
#|   70 GB and 0.3 s the ISLA frontier lies under GeoTransolver's at every
#|   budget, and above it GeoTransolver-1,024 and GeoTransolver-512 with 24
#|   layers sit about 1% below ISLA's best lane here; the figure shows only
#|   the lanes that logged a cost, which is why the ISLA frontier above
#|   70 GB is an upper bound. Data:
#|   results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json and
#|   results/cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json.
#| fig-alt: "Two stacked scatter plots of validation pressure error against training cost, one against peak memory and one against GPU-floor step time, with ISLA points in blue, GeoTransolver in red and Transolver in amber, each with a step-shaped frontier line and labels on the frontier points only."
#| code-fold: true
cfgs = [c for c in ISO.values() if c["status"] == "complete" and c["epochs"] == 500 and c.get("peak_mem_gb") and c.get("step_s_p10")]
# the width and depth ladders add the wider and deeper lanes at 100,000 cells (default slice count)
MODEL_KEY = {"isla": "isla", "gt": "gt_unit", "transolver": "transolver_unit"}
for c in CAPI.values():
    if c["status"] != "complete" or c.get("source") == "ISO-COST" or c["slices"] != 256 or not c.get("peak_mem_gb") or c["pressure_l2_mean"] > 0.1:
        continue
    cfgs.append(dict(model=MODEL_KEY[c["model"]], width=c["width"], cells=100000, epochs=500, lr=c["lr"], params=c["params"], depth=c["depth"],
                     pressure_l2_mean=c["pressure_l2_mean"], pressure_l2_seeds=c["pressure_l2_seeds"], peak_mem_gb=c["peak_mem_gb"],
                     step_s_p10=c["step_s_p10"], step_s_median=c["step_s_median"], status="complete"))
# one record per configuration: the better learning rate where two were run
best = {}
for c in cfgs:
    k = (c["model"], c["width"], c["cells"], c.get("depth", 12 if c["model"] != "transolver_unit" else 8))
    if k not in best or c["pressure_l2_mean"] < best[k]["pressure_l2_mean"]:
        best[k] = c
cfgs = list(best.values())
KEY = {"isla": "isla_ref", "gt_unit": "gt", "transolver_unit": "t"}
def depth_of(c): return c.get("depth", 12 if c["model"] != "transolver_unit" else 8)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(7.2, 7.6), sharey=True)
for ax, axis, xlabel in ((axes[0], "peak_mem_gb", "Peak GPU memory per device [GB]"), (axes[1], "step_s_p10", "GPU-floor step time, p10 [s]")):
    for model in ("isla", "gt_unit", "transolver_unit"):
        pts = sorted([c for c in cfgs if c["model"] == model], key=lambda c: c[axis])
        if not pts:
            continue
        kw = series_kwargs(KEY[model], ls="none")
        ax.plot([c[axis] for c in pts], [c["pressure_l2_mean"] for c in pts], **kw, zorder=3)
        for c in pts:
            ax.plot([c[axis]] * len(c["pressure_l2_seeds"]), c["pressure_l2_seeds"], ls="none", marker="_", color=kw["color"], ms=8, mew=1.1, zorder=4)
        # frontier: best error at or under each budget; label only the lanes that set it
        fx, fy, run, on_front = [], [], float("inf"), []
        for c in pts:
            if c["pressure_l2_mean"] < run:
                on_front.append(c)
            run = min(run, c["pressure_l2_mean"]); fx.append(c[axis]); fy.append(run)
        ax.step(fx, fy, where="post", color=STYLE[KEY[model]]["color"], lw=1.6, alpha=0.55, label="_nolegend_")
        for c in on_front:
            dep = depth_of(c)
            lab = f"{c['width']}x{c['cells'] // 1000}k" + ("" if dep in (8, 12) else f" L{dep}")
            ax.annotate(lab, (c[axis], c["pressure_l2_mean"]), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(6, -10),
                        fontsize=7.5, color=STYLE[KEY[model]]["color"], path_effects=halo())
    d = best.get(("gt_unit", 256, 200000, 12))
    if d:
        ax.plot([d[axis]], [d["pressure_l2_mean"]], marker="o", ms=15, mfc="none", mec=RED, mew=1.4, ls="none", label="GeoTransolver recipe default (256 wide, 200,000 cells)" if ax is axes[0] else "_nolegend_")
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel(xlabel); ax.grid(True, which="both", color=GRID, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
    ticks = [10, 20, 50, 100, 200] if axis == "peak_mem_gb" else [0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0]
    ax.set_xticks(ticks); ax.set_xticklabels([f"{t:g}" for t in ticks]); ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
axes[0].legend(loc="upper right", frameon=False, fontsize=8.2)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## What compute should buy: cases, parameters, epochs {#sec-compute-allocation}

**On the DrivAerML Surface task, below about 200 training cases every unit
of compute belongs to more cases. Past 200 cars the data term of the
fitted law falls below the parameter term and compute goes to width. On
the HiLiftAeroML wings the data term stays above the parameter term over
the whole measured range, 35 to 1,260 wings, so cases remain the better
purchase there, and the same law with the same data exponent for both
architectures is accepted on both datasets. Epochs buy nothing
measurable. On AirfRANS (interior task) the error is a floorless power law
in cases, and cases stay the better purchase across the range measured.**
That is the answer, per dataset, to the question a language-model
practitioner asks of a surrogate: what is the compute-optimal mix of
training set, model size and training length? The instrument is a scaling
study on two surface datasets: ISLA at three widths and GeoTransolver at
three widths, each trained for 500 epochs at 100,000 cells per case, on
27, 54, 109, 218 and 435 DrivAerML cars and on 35, 210, 510 and 1,260
HiLiftAeroML wings, two seeds, scored in float32 (54 configurations).
@fig-scaling-cases shows both pictures with the fitted law drawn where it
is accepted.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scaling-cases
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Surface-pressure error against training cases for three widths of each
#|   model (ISLA at 192, 384 and 768 wide; GeoTransolver at 256, 512 and
#|   1,024), on the DrivAerML Surface task (top; 27 to 435 cars, scored on
#|   the 48 validation cars) and on HiLiftAeroML (bottom; 35 to 1,260 wings,
#|   scored on the 180 validation wings), 500 epochs at 100,000 cells per
#|   case, two-seed means with the seeds as short bars, float32. Lighter
#|   shades are narrower models. Dotted curves are the fitted law
#|   $\varepsilon = \varepsilon_\infty + a n^{-\alpha} + b P^{-\beta}$
#|   evaluated at each width, drawn where the fit meets the 3% acceptance
#|   bar (@tbl-scaling-fit: ISLA on both datasets, GeoTransolver on the
#|   wings only); a gray dashed line is a fitted floor where the fit
#|   identifies one (GeoTransolver's wing fit puts its floor at zero and
#|   carries the floor in a flat parameter term, so none is drawn for it).
#|   How to read this: the vertical spread between shades is what
#|   parameters buy at a given training-set size; the slope is what cases
#|   buy, steep at the small rungs and bending towards a floor at the large
#|   ones on both datasets. Both axes are logarithmic and span each
#|   dataset's measured range. Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json.
#| fig-alt: "Two stacked log-log scatters of pressure error against training cases, DrivAerML from 27 to 435 cars above and HiLiftAeroML from 35 to 1,260 wings below; three blue shades for ISLA widths and three red shades for GeoTransolver widths, dotted fitted curves bending toward a floor where the fit is accepted."
#| code-fold: true
SLD = J("scalelaw_2026-10-08.json")
SL = SLD["configurations"]; SLF = SLD["fits"]
def grid(ds):
    """Per model and width, the (n, two-seed mean, seeds) points of one dataset, and the parameter counts."""
    pts = {"isla": {}, "gt": {}}; params = {"isla": {}, "gt": {}}
    for c in SL.values():
        if c["dataset"] == ds and c["pressure_l2_mean"] and c["status"] == "complete":
            pts[c["model"]].setdefault(c["width"], []).append((c["n"], c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"])); params[c["model"]][c["width"]] = c["params"]
    return pts, params
def mid(a, b):
    return mpl.colors.to_hex((np.array(mpl.colors.to_rgb(a)) + np.array(mpl.colors.to_rgb(b))) / 2)
shades = {"isla": [BLUE_PALE, BLUE_LIGHT, BLUE], "gt": [RED_LIGHT, mid(RED_LIGHT, RED), RED]}
PANELS = (("drivaerml", "DrivAerML Surface task (48 validation cars)", [27, 54, 109, 218, 435], (22, 520), (0.030, 0.165), [0.04, 0.05, 0.07, 0.1, 0.15]),
          ("hilift", "HiLiftAeroML (180 validation wings)", [35, 210, 510, 1260], (28, 1560), (0.024, 0.17), [0.03, 0.04, 0.05, 0.07, 0.1, 0.15]))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 9.0))
for ax, (ds, title, ticks, xlim, ylim, yticks) in zip(axes, PANELS):
    pts, params = grid(ds)
    nn = np.geomspace(xlim[0] * 1.08, xlim[1] * 0.95, 120)
    notes = []
    for m, key in (("isla", "isla_ref"), ("gt", "gt")):
        kw = series_kwargs(key); F = SLF[f"{ds}|{m}"]; f = F["fit"]; accepted = F["law_accepted_rms_below_3pct"]
        for shade, (w, rows) in zip(shades[m], sorted(pts[m].items())):
            rows = sorted(rows); x = [r[0] for r in rows]; y = [r[1] for r in rows]
            ax.plot(x, y, marker=kw["marker"], color=shade, ls="none", ms=6, label=f"{STYLE[key]['label']}, {w} wide")
            for r in rows:
                ax.plot([r[0]] * len(r[2]), r[2], ls="none", marker="_", color=shade, ms=7, mew=1.1)
            if accepted:
                ax.plot(nn, f["eps_inf"] + f["a"] * nn ** (-f["alpha"]) + f["b"] * params[m][w] ** (-f["beta"]), color=shade, ls=":", lw=1.1, zorder=0)
        if accepted and f["eps_inf"] > 1e-6:
            ax.axhline(f["eps_inf"], color=BASELINE, ls="--", lw=0.8, zorder=0)
            ax.text(xlim[0] * 1.15, f["eps_inf"], f"fitted floor {f['eps_inf']:.4f} ({STYLE[key]['label']})", fontsize=7.5, color=INK2, va="bottom", ha="left")
        notes.append(STYLE[key]["label"] if accepted else None)
    ax.plot([], [], color=INK2, ls=":", lw=1.1, label="dotted: fitted law (" + ", ".join(n for n in notes if n) + ")")
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xticks(ticks); ax.set_xticklabels([f"{t:,}" for t in ticks])
    ax.set_yticks(yticks); ax.set_yticklabels([f"{t:.2f}" for t in yticks]); ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
    ax.set_xlim(*xlim); ax.set_ylim(*ylim)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=9.5, loc="left")
    ax.set_xlabel("training cases [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure relative L2 error [–]")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7.4, ncol=2, loc="upper right")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scaling-exponents
#| output: asis
def slope(rows, lo, hi):
    d = {r[0]: r[1] for r in rows}
    return -np.log(d[hi] / d[lo]) / np.log(hi / lo) if lo in d and hi in d else None
DS_NAME = {"drivaerml": "DrivAerML Surface", "hilift": "HiLiftAeroML"}
out = "| dataset | model | width | local exponent of the error against cases, rung to rung | gain of the widest over the narrowest width, by rung |\n|---|---|--:|---|---|\n"
ratios = {}
for ds in ("drivaerml", "hilift"):
    pts, params = grid(ds)
    for m, name in (("isla", "ISLA"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver")):
        ws = sorted(pts[m]); rungs = sorted({r[0] for w in ws for r in pts[m][w]})
        ratios[(ds, m)] = params[m][ws[-1]] / params[m][ws[0]]
        for w in ws:
            rows = pts[m][w]
            cells = "; ".join(f"{a:,} to {b:,}: {s:.2f}" for a, b in zip(rungs, rungs[1:]) for s in [slope(rows, a, b)] if s is not None)
            gains = []
            for n in rungs:
                lo = {r[0]: r[1] for r in pts[m][ws[0]]}.get(n); hi = {r[0]: r[1] for r in pts[m][ws[-1]]}.get(n)
                gains.append(f"{n:,}: {100 * (1 - hi / lo):.0f}%" if lo and hi else f"{n:,}: —")
            out += f"| {DS_NAME[ds]} | {name} | {w} | {cells} | {'; '.join(gains) if w == ws[0] else ''} |\n"
out += (f"\n: Local exponents of the error against training cases on both datasets (the negative log-log slope between adjacent rungs, at each width) and the gain at each rung from the widest over the narrowest lane "
        f"(a {ratios[('drivaerml', 'isla')]:.0f}x parameter increase for ISLA and {ratios[('drivaerml', 'gt')]:.0f}x for GeoTransolver). How to read this: a falling local exponent is the signature of an approach to a floor, not of a scale-free law; "
        "the wings fall from about 0.5 to about 0.1 to 0.2 over 35 to 1,260 cases where the cars fall from about 0.7 to 0.1 over 27 to 435. A negative gain is a rung where the widest lane is not the best. "
        "Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json. {#tbl-scaling-exponents}\n")
print(out)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scaling-fit
#| output: asis
out = "| dataset | model | $\\varepsilon_\\infty$ | $a$ | $\\alpha$ | $b$ | $\\beta$ | RMS residual | accepted (below 3%) | $n^\\ast$ at the scaling study's base width (192 for ISLA, 256 for GeoTransolver) |\n|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|--:|\n"
UNIT = {"drivaerml": "cars", "hilift": "wings"}
for ds in ("drivaerml", "hilift"):
    for m, name in (("isla", "ISLA"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver")):
        F = SLF[f"{ds}|{m}"]; f = F["fit"]; b = F["bootstrap_p16_p50_p84"]
        rng_ = lambda k: f"{f[k]:.2f} ({b[k][0]:.2f} to {b[k][2]:.2f})"
        floor = f"{f['eps_inf']:.4f} ({b['eps_inf'][0]:.4f} to {b['eps_inf'][2]:.4f})" + (" (on its upper bound)" if f["eps_inf_on_bound"] else (" (at zero: the floor sits in the flat parameter term)" if f["eps_inf"] < 1e-6 else ""))
        bval = f"{f['b']:.0f}" if f["b"] >= 10 else f"{f['b']:.2f}"
        out += f"| {DS_NAME[ds]} | {name} | {floor} | {f['a']:.1f} | {rng_('alpha')} | {bval} | {rng_('beta')} | {100 * f['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}% | {'yes' if F['law_accepted_rms_below_3pct'] else 'no'} | {F['n_star_recipe_width']:,.0f} {UNIT[ds]} |\n"
out += ("\n: The fitted law $\\varepsilon = \\varepsilon_\\infty + a\\,n^{-\\alpha} + b\\,P^{-\\beta}$ per architecture and dataset (least squares on the relative residual of the seed means; $\\varepsilon_\\infty$ bounded to at most 0.9 times the best measured error; 16th to 84th percentiles of a 400-draw two-seed bootstrap in parentheses). "
        "A fit is accepted when its RMS relative residual is below 3%. $n^\\ast$ is the case count at which the data and parameter terms are equal at the scaling study's base width (ISLA 192, GeoTransolver 256). "
        "How to read this: GeoTransolver's DrivAerML row is reported but not accepted, so its exponents are indicative and its curve is not drawn in @fig-scaling-cases. With three widths per model $\\beta$ is weakly identified on every row (its bootstrap range says so), and GeoTransolver's wing fit uses that freedom to put the floor into the parameter term: $\\beta$ near zero makes $b\\,P^{-\\beta}$ a constant of about 0.03 at these widths and $\\varepsilon_\\infty$ falls to zero, so its wing $n^\\ast$ is the case count at which the data term drops below that constant, not a crossover between cases and parameters. "
        "Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json. {#tbl-scaling-fit}\n")
print(out)
```

```{python}
H = {m: SLF[f"hilift|{m}"] for m in ("isla", "gt")}; Dd = {m: SLF[f"drivaerml|{m}"] for m in ("isla", "gt")}
hp, _ = grid("hilift")
best1260 = {m: min(((w, {r[0]: r[1] for r in rows}[1260]) for w, rows in hp[m].items()), key=lambda t: t[1]) for m in ("isla", "gt")}
gain_h = {m: H[m]["gain_widest_over_narrowest_by_n"] for m in ("isla", "gt")}
print(f"**Reading the exponents.** The error is not a single power law in the "
      f"training-set size on either dataset. On the cars the local exponent falls from about 0.7 to 0.9 between 27 and 54 cars to 0.1 to 0.2 between 218 and 435, "
      f"and on the wings from about 0.5 between 35 and 210 wings to {min(v['510-1260'] for m in ('isla', 'gt') for v in H[m]['alpha_local_by_width'].values()):.1f} to "
      f"{max(v['510-1260'] for m in ('isla', 'gt') for v in H[m]['alpha_local_by_width'].values()):.1f} between 510 and 1,260, for both models (@tbl-scaling-exponents). "
      f"That is the signature of an approach to a floor, and on the cars the floor is the one @sec-shared-floor measures directly. "
      f"The fitted data exponent is {Dd['isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} to {Dd['gt']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} on the cars and {H['isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} to {H['gt']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} on the wings, "
      f"the two architectures within {max(abs(Dd['isla']['fit']['alpha'] - Dd['gt']['fit']['alpha']), abs(H['isla']['fit']['alpha'] - H['gt']['fit']['alpha'])):.2f} of each other on both (@tbl-scaling-fit): "
      f"the wing error approaches its floor more slowly in the case count, and how fast it approaches is a property of the dataset, not of the architecture. "
      f"ISLA's fitted floors are {Dd['isla']['fit']['eps_inf']:.4f} on the cars and {H['isla']['fit']['eps_inf']:.4f} on the wings. "
      f"Parameters are cheap by comparison at every rung. On the cars a 15x increase buys each model about a tenth of its error from 54 cars up, and the capacity ladders show that a further doubling at 435 cars buys a few percent before turning over; "
      f"on the wings the same increase buys ISLA {100 * min(gain_h['isla'].values()):.0f} to {100 * max(gain_h['isla'].values()):.0f}% by rung and GeoTransolver nothing at 35 and 210 wings and {100 * min(gain_h['gt']['510'], gain_h['gt']['1260']):.0f} to {100 * max(gain_h['gt']['510'], gain_h['gt']['1260']):.0f}% above. "
      f"At 1,260 wings the best ISLA lane is the {best1260['isla'][0]}-wide one at {best1260['isla'][1]:.4f}, the first rung at which its widest lane is not its best, and GeoTransolver's {best1260['gt'][0]}-wide lane leads the grid at {best1260['gt'][1]:.4f}. "
      f"The compute-optimal crossover at the base width, where the fitted data and parameter terms are equal, is {Dd['isla']['n_star_recipe_width']:.0f} cars for ISLA and {H['isla']['n_star_recipe_width']:,.0f} wings, beyond the measured range, so on the wings every unit of compute belongs to cases throughout the range measured. "
      f"Epochs are the third axis, and they are converged (@sec-equal-budget).")
```

**The fitted law.** With five rungs and three widths the Chinchilla form
$\varepsilon = \varepsilon_\infty + a\,n^{-\alpha} + b\,P^{-\beta}$ is
identifiable for ISLA (@tbl-scaling-fit). The floor lands inside its
allowed range, and the fit reproduces the fifteen seed means to
`{python} f"{100 * SLF['drivaerml|isla']['fit']['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}%"`
RMS, under the 3% acceptance bar set in advance. The exponents describe
the *reducible* error above the floor, which is why $\alpha$ is far above
the local slopes of the total error in @tbl-scaling-exponents. For
GeoTransolver the same form misses the bar
(`{python} f"{100 * SLF['drivaerml|gt']['fit']['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}%"`)
and pushes the floor onto its bound. The cause is that its 27-car rung is
not monotone in width (the 1,024-wide model is worse than the 512-wide one
there, seeds separated), and an additive law has no term for a wide model
losing to a narrower one at small data. Its exponents are nonetheless
within the bootstrap spread of ISLA's
(`{python} "same" if SLD['bars']['drivaerml']['exponents_same']['alpha']['same'] and SLD['bars']['drivaerml']['exponents_same']['beta']['same'] else "different"`
within the bootstrap on both). **The two architectures convert cases and
parameters into accuracy at the same rates on this task.**
GeoTransolver's small-data lead (@sec-data-efficiency) is an offset in
the coefficients, not a slope. ISLA shows the same non-monotonicity in
milder form at 27 cars, so the effect is not one architecture's.

**Width lowers the curve without steepening it.** The scaling study above
runs at 100,000 cells with the narrower ISLA widths. The reporting
protocol's training-car ladder (@sec-car-ladder), which holds ISLA at 384
wide, 12 layers, 256 slices, 5e-4, gives the same reading.
@tbl-refboard-exponents puts the learning-curve exponent of the total
error over 27 to 218 cars (the negative log-log slope of a least-squares
line through the four seed means) beside the 192-wide lanes and the
baselines. The 384-wide lane is 5 to 10% below the 192-wide lane at every
rung with the same exponent, so what width bought on this dataset is an offset, exactly
as GeoTransolver's small-data lead is an offset. These are exponents of
the total error, which is why they sit near 0.5 rather than at the
fitted law's $\alpha \approx 1.3$ for the reducible part.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-refboard-exponents
#| output: asis
RBN = {"isla_r1": "ISLA (384 wide, 5e-4)", "isla_192": "ISLA, 192 wide (1e-3)", "gt256_lr3e3": "GeoTransolver-256 (3e-3)",
       "gt256": "GeoTransolver-256 (1e-3)", "transolver256": "Transolver-256 (3e-3)"}
out = "| configuration | 27 cars | 54 | 109 | 218 | exponent, 27 to 218 cars |\n|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|\n"
for a, name in RBN.items():
    b = "**" if a == "isla_r1" else ""
    out += f"| {b}{name}{b} | " + " | ".join(f"{b}{RBS[f'{a}|n{n}']['mean']:.4f}{b}" for n in (27, 54, 109, 218)) + f" | {b}{RBX[a]['exponent']:.2f}{b} |\n"
r1_over_192 = [RBS[f"isla_r1|n{n}"]["mean"] / RBS[f"isla_192|n{n}"]["mean"] for n in (27, 54, 109, 218)]
print(out)
print(f": The training-car ladder of the DrivAerML Surface task at the reporting protocol (200,000 cells per case, 500 epochs, two-seed "
      f"means, float32 on the 48 validation cars) and the learning-curve exponent of each configuration's total error over 27 to 218 cars. "
      f"The 384-wide lane's error is {100 * (1 - max(r1_over_192)):.0f} to {100 * (1 - min(r1_over_192)):.0f}% below the "
      f"192-wide lane's at every rung. How to read this: the exponents are of the total error and are local to this range. The fitted law "
      f"of @tbl-scaling-fit separates the floor from the reducible error and is the statement about mechanism. GeoTransolver's exponent at "
      f"1e-3 is larger only because that rate starts from a worse 27-car error. Data: results/refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json. "
      f"{{#tbl-refboard-exponents}}")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-exponents-datasets
#| output: asis
steeper = [r for r in ROWS if r[1] > r[2] * 1.05 and "equal steps" not in r[0]]
flatter = [r for r in ROWS if r[2] > r[1] * 1.05 and "equal steps" not in r[0]]
same = [r for r in ROWS if r not in steeper and r not in flatter and "equal steps" not in r[0]]
name = lambda r: r[0].split(",")[0] + " (" + r[0].split(", ")[1] + ")"
lst = lambda rs: ", ".join(name(r) for r in rs) if rs else "none"
print(f"**Across the datasets with a training-case ladder, ISLA's error falls faster with cases than GeoTransolver's on "
      f"{len(steeper)} of {len(steeper) + len(flatter) + len(same)} fields, at the same rate on {len(same)}, and slower on {len(flatter)}.** "
      f"Steeper: {lst(steeper)}. Same rate (within 5%): {lst(same)}. Slower: {lst(flatter)}. "
      "On the DrivAerML Surface task both architectures approach one floor, so the total-error exponents there understate the "
      "reducible-error law of @tbl-scaling-fit. Tensile2d has no training-case ladder, so it is absent "
      "here. A steeper curve is what a model with the right inductive bias shows "
      "while the data are scarce for the problem's variation, which is why the ladders, and not one full-data row, are the evidence "
      "for or against the architecture.")
```

**The compute-optimal rule this implies.** Training compute in this
recipe is proportional to parameters times tokens seen, $C \propto P
\cdot n \cdot c \cdot E$ with $n$ cases, $c$ cells per case and $E$
epochs. Cells are flat above 100,000 and epochs are converged
(@sec-equal-budget), so the question reduces to $P$ against $n$ at fixed
$P \cdot n$. In the Chinchilla form the optimum grows the axis with the
*smaller* exponent once the other's term is driven down, $P^\ast \propto
C^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}$ and $n^\ast \propto C^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)}$.
With ISLA's $\alpha \approx 1.3$ and $\beta \approx 0.5$ this puts about
70% of each compute increment into parameters *once the data term is the
smaller one*. The crossover is where the two fitted terms are equal
at the scaling study's base width, 192 for ISLA:
`{python} f"{SLF['drivaerml|isla']['n_star_recipe_width']:.0f}"` cars
for ISLA (@tbl-scaling-fit). Below that count the data term dominates and
every unit of compute belongs to cases. Above it the residual data term
is a few thousandths and compute goes to width or depth until the floor.
The rule in one line: *collect cases until about 200, then widen.* Two
practical consequences follow. On a dataset of a few hundred cases the
recipe's width is the right place to spend. A claim that one architecture
"scales better" needs the exponents, not a single-width ladder.

**The same axis on a second dataset and task.** On AirfRANS (the interior
task of @sec-airfrans) the training-case axis runs over nested subsets of
50 to 800 airfoils, and the curve has a different shape: no floor is within
reach at 800 airfoils, ISLA's error falls as a clean power law on pressure
and velocity, and on the one task where the two architectures' exponents
differ ISLA has the larger one (@sec-airfrans-ladder, @fig-scaling-airfrans).
Two consequences follow for the rule above. First, the exponents are
properties of a dataset and a task, not of an architecture, and do not
transfer; a compute-allocation rule must be measured where it will be
used. Second, the compute-optimal crossover moves with the exponent: with
no floor and an exponent well below one, the data term never becomes
small, and cases stay the better purchase across the whole AirfRANS range
measured.

## Cost {#sec-cost-sweep}


```{python}
#| label: setup-cost
#| include: false
import statistics as st
CSR = J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")
CS = CSR["runs"]
GIB_TO_GB = 1024 ** 3 / 1e9
at200 = {r["arm"]: r for r in CS if r["tokens"] == 200000 and r["status"] == "ok"}
def cost(arm):
    r = at200[arm]; return st.median(r["step_ms"]), r["peak_allocated_gib"], r["n_params"]
c_isla, c_r2, c_i192, c_g256, c_g512, c_t = (cost(a) for a in ("isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused", "isla_ref_r2_384x24_cos_fused", "isla_192x12_cos_fused",
                                                                   "geotransolver_256", "geotransolver_512", "transolver_256"))
```

```{python}
#| label: para-cost-lede
#| output: asis
print(f"**On the DrivAerML Surface task at the reporting protocol the cost sweep holds ISLA at 384 wide, 12 layers, 256 slices against the 256- "
      f"and 512-wide baselines: GeoTransolver-256 is {(1 - refm('isla_r1|dr435') / GT256_435) * 100:.0f}% less accurate than that ISLA at "
      f"{c_g256[1] / c_isla[1]:.2f}x its memory, and GeoTransolver-512 is as accurate at {c_g512[1] / c_isla[1]:.2f}x its memory and "
      f"{c_g512[0] / c_isla[0]:.2f}x its step time (the ladders' configurations, @sec-car-ladder; the reference configurations' training "
      f"footprints are in @sec-using-cost).** The per-configuration footprints are @tbl-isla-cost; what the token budget does to them is @fig-cost-sweep. Every arm "
      "is linear in tokens above 100,000, because the slice attention is linear in points and no quadratic term appears up to 600,000, and "
      "every arm is launch-bound below about 40,000, where the GPU is not saturated. ISLA's step is with the fused geometry kernel "
      "(`geo_kernel=None` resolves to it on CUDA, @sec-using-cost); on the fallback eager geometry region, whose per-slice invariants are "
      "recomputed in the backward pass, the step grows linearly from 20,000 tokens on and is several times GeoTransolver's at 200,000. At "
      f"the recipe default of 200,000 cells every model fits one GB300, and the narrowest ISLA at 192 wide ({c_i192[2] / 1e6:.1f}M, "
      f"{c_i192[0]:.0f} ms, {c_i192[1]:.1f} GiB) is the cheapest model per token after Transolver: at 600,000 cells its training-log peak is "
      f"{ISO['isla|w192|c600k|lr1e-3|ep500']['peak_mem_gb']:.0f} GB, about what GeoTransolver-256 needs at 200,000 "
      f"({ISO['gt_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500']['peak_mem_gb']:.0f} GB).")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-cost-sweep
```
